name: Task_7
description:
Evaluate the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient (\u03b2) of bulk Aluminum between 300 K and 500 K using molecular dynamics. Use the MACE-MP-0 foundation model as the ASE-compatible calculator. Start with a conventional FCC unit cell of Aluminum (a = 4.05 \u00c5) and replicate it into a 3 \u00d7 3 \u00d7 3 supercell. Conduct molecular dynamics simulations in the isothermal-isobaric (NPT) ensemble at target temperatures of 300 K, 400 K, and 500 K, and an external pressure of 1.01325 bar. For each temperature, equilibrate for at least 2 ps and retain at least 3 ps of production, extending both until temperature, volume, and pressure are settled and well sampled. Use IsotropicMTKNPT or NPTBerendsen for isotropic pressure control, choose suitable thermostat and barostat settings, and use an integration timestep no larger than 2 fs. Record at least 32 production samples per stage, spaced at most 100 fs apart, to compute the average volume at each temperature. Use an unweighted linear fit of heating mean volume against measured mean temperature over 300–500 K, divided by the heating 300 K mean volume, to extract the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient. Report the resulting coefficient in K⁻¹, and retain the calculation.

Run one continuous heating sequence through 300, 400, and 500 K followed by cooling through 400 and 300 K, initializing velocities only once and preserving positions, cell, and momenta. Add a heating stage on each side of 400 K, 5–50 K away, to estimate the local expansion coefficient from all heating stages within 50 K of 400 K. Independently estimate the bulk modulus and local expansion coefficient from fixed-cell NVT pressure measurements near 400 K and the heating 400 K mean volume, varying both temperature and volume. The evaluator derives both local coefficients, their pressure-minus-volume difference, and the cooling-minus-heating volume differences at 300 and 400 K; agreement is not assumed.
